# What can eligible-only published scores establish about stale queues?

Secondary identification analysis following inspection of the published-capacity replay. Fix Sánchez Trujillo et al.'s day-84 temporal population, all eight score exports, 857 pooled seats, and the original six status scenarios. A stale admission with a dated exit is an ineligible contact with zero subsequent-case utility. With m such admissions missing model scores, the number of eligible seats is between max(0,857−m) and 857. Permitting any missing probability in [0,1], calculate lower and upper expected actionable capture from these two eligible prefixes. Average uniformly across ties at a cutoff. Check that valid endpoint probabilities can place every stale admission below or above all eligible scores. Verify both bounds by explicitly completing the queue in the two extreme ways. Compare the bounds with the exact expected count of uniform review over each admitted pool. No minimum benefit is introduced. Report every model and delay. Bounds condition on the published records and missing-score assumption; they are not sampling intervals.
